cited_evidence: Top-level corpus and Job 2 input needs are demand-descending: n06-r01 has demand_score 9, n06-r02 has 8, ... n06-r08 has 3.
Job 2 input evidence_sources instead ranks n06-r08 as rank 1, n06-r07 as rank 2, and n06-r01 as rank 8, contradicting the required demand-descending rank order.
Job 2 output priorities preserve the supplied upstream_rank order: unsupported n06-r07 with upstream_rank 2 is priority_rank 1, while unsupported n06-r01 with upstream_rank 8 is priority_rank 2.
The package provides job identities but no function names, so exact function localization is not supported by the visible evidence.
initial_receipt.explanation: The downstream job appears to preserve the supplied handoffs and ranks priorities using the upstream_rank values it received. The fault is already present in the upstream evidence_sources handoff: its rank order is not demand-descending relative to the top-level corpus/needs, so Job 2 inherits that incorrect provenance order and recommends n06-r07 ahead of the higher-demand unsupported n06-r01.
